embroidery.description: A free web tool for drafting Karelian embroidery patterns on a stitch grid and downloading them as a PDF.
embroidery.title: Karelian Embroidery Designer
embroidery.lead: A web tool for drafting Karelian embroidery patterns.
embroidery.photoAlt: An embroidered bookmark: white Karelian-style birds and spirals stitched on blue fabric
embroidery.screenshotAlt: Screenshot of the Karelian Embroidery Designer: a toolbar of stitch tools above a grid with a bird motif drawn in red
features: Draw on a stitch grid with straight, diagonal and cross stitches
Set the width and height of the pattern
Undo mistakes or start over with a clean grid
Download the finished pattern as a PDF
embroidery.tradition: Karelian embroidery is a traditional counted-thread technique from Karelia. The stitches follow the threads of an even-weave fabric and build up geometric motifs: rhombuses, crosses, branches and birds. Embroidery is traditionally in red on white linen.
embroidery.closingTitle: Ready to draft your own pattern?

knitting.description: An upcoming tool for designing knitting charts and patterns from measurements.
knitting.title: Knitting Pattern Generator
knitting.lead: A tool for designing your own projects based on your measurements and gauge.
knitting.photoAlt: A sock in progress on double-pointed needles, with a green and grey colourwork pattern
plans: Choose a project, like socks, mittens or a hat
Enter your measurements and the size you want
Swatch, then enter your gauge in stitches and rows per 10 cm
Get a written pattern with your stitch and row counts worked out
Print it or save it as a PDF to knit from

designer.description: Draw Karelian embroidery patterns on a stitch grid: drag along the grid lines, use traditional motifs as templates and download your pattern as a picture.
designer.title: Karelian Embroidery Designer

tools.label: Tools
tools.pan: Hand: move around (H, or hold Space)

designer.fit: Fit the grid to the view

pen.title: Pen
pen.hint: Drag along the grid lines or diagonals; the pen follows the holes in the linen. Tap a line to add or remove one stitch.

shape.title: Cell shapes
shape.hint: Click a cell, or drag across cells to stitch a row.

erase.title: Eraser
erase.hint: Drag over stitches to unpick them.

pan.title: Hand
pan.hint: Drag to move around the grid. With any tool, hold Space or use the scrollbars.

select.title: Select
select.hint: Drag a rectangle over the grid. Then drag inside it to move it, or use the buttons. Esc clears the selection.
select.moveHint: Drag inside the dashed box to move it, or use the arrow keys.

placing.title: Placing: {name}
placing.hint: Click the grid to place it. R turns it, Esc stops.
placing.templateHint: Click the grid to place it, as many times as you like. R turns it, Esc stops.

templates.title: Templates
templates.hint: Pick a motif, then click the grid to place it. You can turn or mirror it first.

grid.title: Grid size
grid.hint: 4 to 200 cells. Stitches outside a smaller grid are removed, and undo starts over.

yoke.description: Work out the numbers for a top-down round yoke sweater from your gauge and measurements: cast-on, increase rounds, body and sleeves.
yoke.title: Round yoke sweater calculator
yoke.lead: For a sweater knitted from the top down with a round yoke. Enter your gauge and measurements, and the stitch and round counts are worked out as you type.
yoke.example: The form starts with example values. Replace them with your own; they're remembered in this browser.

form.gaugeHint: Knit a swatch and count over 10 cm.
form.measurementsHint: Body measurements in cm, taken over the clothes you'll wear under the sweater.
form.yokeLengthHint: From the neckline to the underarm
form.easeHint: How much bigger than the body the sweater is, in cm. A regular fit is about 5 cm.
form.underarmHint: Width cast on under each arm, in cm.
form.increasesHint: How many stitches each increase round adds.
form.neckRaise: Raise the back of the neck with short rows

results.title: Your numbers
results.incomplete: Fill in the fields marked above to see the numbers.
results.increaseCountLast: {count} rounds of {n} increases, the last one {last}
results.yokeEnd: At the bottom of the yoke
results.turns: First turns {first} stitches either side of the centre back, then {step} stitches further out each time
results.turnsOne: Turn {first} stitches either side of the centre back
results.neckRaiseNote: Work them before the yoke increases. They add height at the back only.
results.finishedNote: From the rounded counts, in cm.

warnings.neckTooBig: The neckline is as wide as the bottom of the yoke, so there's nothing to increase. Check the neckline, bust and upper arm measurements.
warnings.tooFewIncreases: {n} increases per round won't fit into the yoke. Use at least {minimum}, or a longer yoke.
warnings.increasesEveryRound: This needs increases on consecutive rounds. More increases per round spread them out.
warnings.shortRowsDontFit: The back neck raise is too tall for this neckline. Try a lower one.
warnings.moreIncreasesThanStitches: There are more increases per round than stitches at the neck. Use fewer increases per round.

about.description: About Aada Härmä: web tools for fibre arts, studies at Tampere University and all kinds of handcraft.
about.title: About me
about.lead: I'm Aada, also known as BoingoDuck on the internet. I build small web tools that make pattern design easier and more accessible to everyone.
paragraphs: I recently graduated as a Bachelor of Science and am now continuing in the master's programme at Tampere University, majoring in communications engineering with a minor in economics.
Outside of tech I love all kinds of handcraft, from knitting to wood carving.
For now, this site focuses on fibre arts, but I'd like to branch out into other crafts in the future.
about.portraitAlt: Aada knitting with red needles, framed in a red and white embroidery hoop
